recommendation.headline: TVS iQube, tentatively, mainly because the evidence argues against Ola on your top priority
recommendation.summary: Evidence on reliability and service for Ather, TVS and Bajaj is thin; Ola's service problems are well documented, so a established-maker scooter such as the iQube is the safer pick pending test rides.

reasons.text: Ola has documented service problems (80,000 complaints a month, 30-45 day waits).
iQube Power mode reaches indicated 80kph and the scooter has good ergonomics.
Bigger-battery iQube variants offer decent range for daily use.

tradeoffs.text: Aggressive regen and no verified Bengaluru service data for TVS.

alternatives.when: you want best handling and are not tall or comfort-focused
only if you accept service risk

caveats: No source gives measured real-world range or Bengaluru service-centre counts for non-Ola brands
nextSteps: Check local service centre distance and owner reviews

contradictions.assessment: Autocar (direct test) says Power mode hits indicated 80kph; source 2 says it runs out of breath near 60. Source 2 appears to rewrite Autocar with changed details, so Autocar is preferred, though it is from 2022.

contradictions.topic: Ola complaints volume and Eco mode
contradictions.assessment: Source 2 says 8,000 complaints a month and Eco mode fine; three sources say 80,000 and Autocar says Eco is dangerous. Majority and primary reporting preferred.

uncertainties.text: No service or reliability evidence for Ather, TVS, Bajaj in Bengaluru
uncertainties.howToResolve: Check owner forums and service centre locations

uncertainties.text: iQube range claim from one undated page
